topics.title: 课程作业
topics.summary: 麦吉尔没有默认的全校许可或禁令。根据守则第 25(b) 条，学生不得以未经教师或导师授权、或违反课程 AI 要求的方式在考核中使用生成式 AI；使用课程大纲或书面说明禁止的工具属于作弊（第 26(f) 条）。教师应在课程大纲中写明 AI 规则。
topics.scope: 守则第 25(b)、26(f) 条；课程大纲声明。

claims.text: McGill's Code of Student Conduct and Disciplinary Procedures (current version effective November 12, 2025) states that no student may use generative AI in an assessment in a manner not authorized by the relevant instructor or supervisor, or that violates the course's AI requirements (Article 25(b)), and that using any tool, including generative AI, that has been disallowed in the course outline or written assessment instructions is cheating (Article 26(f)). AI-detection software is not sufficient by itself to substantiate an allegation under Article 25. Permission is therefore set by the instructor, supervisor and course, not university-wide.

evidence.quote: No Student may use generative AI in the context of an Assessment in a manner not authorized by the relevant instructor or supervisor, or in a manner that violates any requirements regarding the use of AI in the context of a given course. AI-detection software is not sufficient, by itself, to substantiate an allegation under this article of the Code.

claims.text: McGill's Principles on Generative AI in Teaching and Learning state (fifth principle) that students remain responsible for academic rigour: verifying the accuracy of AI-generated information, acknowledging the use of generative AI tools where applicable, informing themselves about and complying with instructors' explicit expectations, and respecting limits set on AI use in assessment tasks. Whether AI is allowed or prohibited is not set university-wide.

evidence.quote: Fifth principle: Students remain responsible for maintaining academic rigour. This involves both verifying the accuracy of information generated and acknowledging the use of generative AI tools, if applicable. Students are responsible for informing themselves about and complying with instructors’ explicit expectations and must respect limits established about the use of generative AI tools in assessment tasks.
evidence.title: Principles on Generative AI in Teaching and Learning at McGill
evidence.location: Fifth principle; physical PDF page 2; lines 65-69 of captured PDF text

claims.text: McGill recommends that instructors explain to students in their course outline what the appropriate use or non-use is of generative AI tools in the context of that course. The use or non-use of these tools should align with the learning outcomes associated with the course.

evidence.quote: There should be no default assumption as to the use of generative AI tools. Therefore, McGill recommends that instructors explain to students in their course outline what the appropriate use or non-use is of generative AI tools in the context of that course. The use or non-use of these tools should align with the learning outcomes associated with the course. For this reason, instructors will need to write their own context-appropriate course outline statements.

claims.text: McGill Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies research guidelines (November 2024) sort graduate students' AI uses into three tiers: low-to-moderate risk (e.g. proofreading, light editing, debugging existing code, formatting references), moderate-to-high risk (generating content for one's own use, such as summaries for personal study), and very high risk (generating content and presenting it as one's own work, which constitutes plagiarism under the Code of Student Conduct, e.g. writing entire sections). claims.text: Under McGill's Code, no allegation is substantiated unless the University proves it on a Balance of Probabilities, and the student is entitled to have an Advisor present at any interview or hearing under the Code. A party wishing to appeal a decision of the CSD Hearing Committee must notify the Secretary of the Appeal Committee within 10 Days (working days under the Code) of receiving official notice of that decision; this deadline applies to CSD Hearing Committee decisions, not to every academic decision. Appeals are limited to new evidence, procedural error or bias, or fundamental error in interpreting offences or applying sanctions.

claims.text: McGill IT Services states that, unless formally reviewed and approved by McGill, it is prohibited to use any generative AI tool for McGill-related purposes; new AI tools, AI features added to existing platforms and requests involving sensitive data go through the AI Review Committee process. For translating McGill content, Linguistic Services lists two approved tools - DeepL Pro (paid version) and Microsoft Copilot (enterprise version) - with the free versions prohibited for data-security reasons and no private or sensitive information to be entered. These are institutional data and translation rules, not course permissions.
